summary: Defines the UIDPLUS extension of IMAP, a set of features that reduce the time and resources used by certain client operations. They are mainly meant for clients that sometimes work offline. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: UIDPLUS is a set of small additions to IMAP for clients that are not always connected. It adds a command that deletes only the messages you name, and response codes that tell you the identifiers of messages the server has just copied or stored for you.

questions: what is the appenduid response code
subtitle: Small IMAP additions that tell a client the UIDs of messages it just copied or appended, and let it expunge only chosen messages.

tldr.problem: A client that has been offline for a while cannot tell which messages another client deleted while it was away, so resynchronising risks throwing away mail that is still wanted.
tldr.mechanism: The document adds one command, UID EXPUNGE, which removes only the messages the client names, and three response codes. APPENDUID and COPYUID tell the client the UIDs of messages it has just appended or copied, and UIDNOTSTICKY warns that a mailbox cannot keep UIDs at all.
tldr.outcome: A disconnected client can pick up where it left off without deleting the wrong messages, and it can learn the new UIDs of its own copies without fetching the mailbox again. The document replaced RFC 2359 in 2005.

facts.label: UIDNOTSTICKY is returned in
facts.value: An untagged NO response to SELECT

facts.label: APPENDUID and COPYUID are returned in
facts.value: A tagged OK response to APPEND and COPY

today: RFC 4315 is a Proposed Standard on the IETF Standards Track. It replaced RFC 2359 in 2005, adding the UIDNOTSTICKY response code, and it has not itself been obsoleted or updated. It extends IMAP itself, defined in RFC 3501.

sections.title: What UIDPLUS Adds
sections.content:
The UIDPLUS extension is present in any IMAP server that returns "UIDPLUS" as one of the supported capabilities to the CAPABILITY command. It defines one additional command, and it recommends new status response codes that should be returned by all server implementations whether or not the extension itself is implemented.

The features are optimizations. A client can provide equivalent functionality, less efficiently, using the facilities of the base protocol. The primary audience is the disconnected-use client: one that is not connected all the time and has to catch up when it reconnects.

The document uses "UID set" in a sense similar to the IMAP sequence set, with one difference: the asterisk wildcard that stands for the highest sequence number is not permitted in a UID set.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension is aimed at clients that connect only now and then. Everything in it is an optimization: a client could get the same effect with the original IMAP commands, just more slowly.

sections.title: The UID EXPUNGE Command
sections.content:
UID EXPUNGE takes a sequence set as its argument. It permanently removes, from the currently selected mailbox, all messages that both have the \Deleted flag set and have a UID included in the sequence set. A message that either does not have the flag or has a UID outside the set is not affected. The command answers OK when the expunge is complete, NO when it fails, for example because permission was denied, and BAD when the command is unknown or its arguments are invalid.

The command is particularly useful for disconnected clients. By using UID EXPUNGE instead of EXPUNGE when resynchronising with the server, the client can be sure it does not inadvertently remove messages that other clients marked \Deleted between the time the client was last connected and the time it resynchronises.

If the server does not support the UIDPLUS capability, the client should fall back to using the STORE command to temporarily remove the \Deleted flag from the messages it does not want to remove, then issue the EXPUNGE command, and finally use STORE to restore the flag on the messages where it was temporarily removed. Alternatively the client may fall back to just the EXPUNGE command, risking the unintended removal of some messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The command removes only the messages you name, and only those already flagged for deletion. That way a client that was offline cannot wipe out mail that another client deleted in the meantime.

sections.title: The Three Response Codes
sections.content:
APPENDUID is followed by the UIDVALIDITY of the destination mailbox and the UID assigned to the appended message, and is returned in a tagged OK response to the APPEND command. If the server also supports the MULTIAPPEND extension and several messages were appended, the second value is a UID set of the assigned UIDs, in the order they were transmitted. That set must not contain extraneous UIDs or the asterisk wildcard. The UID set form must not be used when only a single message was appended, and in particular a server must not send a range such as 123:123, because a client that does not support MULTIAPPEND expects only a single UID.

COPYUID is followed by the UIDVALIDITY of the destination mailbox, a UID set of the messages in the source mailbox that were copied, and a UID set of the UIDs assigned in the destination mailbox. The source set is in the order the messages were copied and the destination set corresponds to it in the same order, and neither may contain extraneous UIDs or the asterisk wildcard. It is returned in a tagged OK response to the COPY command.

UIDNOTSTICKY says that the selected mailbox is backed by a mail store that does not support persistent UIDs, so UIDVALIDITY will be different each time the mailbox is selected and APPEND or COPY to it returns no APPENDUID or COPYUID. It is returned in an untagged NO response to the SELECT command. Servers should not have UIDNOTSTICKY mail stores; the facility exists to support legacy stores where persistent UIDs are technically infeasible.
sections.plainLanguage: After an append or a copy, the server tells the client the identifiers of the new messages. The third code is the opposite: it says this mailbox cannot remember identifiers at all, so the client knows not to trust them.

sections.title: A Worked Exchange
sections.content:
The document's example appends a message to the mailbox saved-messages and the server answers with OK [APPENDUID 38505 3955], so the appended message has UID 3955 in a mailbox whose UIDVALIDITY is 38505. The next command copies messages 2 to 4 into the mailbox meeting, and the server answers OK [COPYUID 38505 304,319:320 3956:3958]. The source set names the UIDs that were copied and the destination set names the UIDs they were given.

A third command, UID COPY 305:310, copies nothing and the server answers that no messages matched. The example explains why: message 2 had UID 304 and message 3 had UID 319, so the UIDs from 305 to 310 do not exist. A fourth command copies a single message into the mailbox funny and gets no COPYUID, and the SELECT of that mailbox then shows a UIDVALIDITY and the response NO [UIDNOTSTICKY] Non-persistent UIDs, so the store behind it cannot keep UIDs from one session to the next.
sections.plainLanguage: The example walks through the four cases: a copy that returns new identifiers, a copy that matches nothing, a copy that returns no identifiers, and a mailbox that says its identifiers do not last.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content:
The syntax is given in ABNF, extending the ABNF rules of the IMAP specification, and the IMAP4 rules should be imported before the rules here are validated. The capability list gains "UIDPLUS", the select command gains the alternative uid-expunge, and the response codes gain resp-code-apnd, which is "APPENDUID" followed by a non-zero number and an append-uid, and resp-code-copy, which is "COPYUID" followed by a non-zero number and two UID sets.

A uid-set is a comma-separated list of single identifiers or ranges, and a uid-range holds two identifiers with every value between them regardless of order, so 2:4 and 4:2 are equivalent. A server that supports MULTIAPPEND extends the append-uid rule to allow a UID set, but only where the client has used MULTIAPPEND to append several messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The document gives the exact grammar so that implementations agree on the spelling of the command and the codes, including how a range of identifiers is written.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The COPYUID and APPENDUID response codes return information about the mailbox, which may be considered sensitive if the mailbox has permissions that let the client COPY or APPEND to it but not SELECT or EXAMINE it. The codes should therefore not be issued if the client does not have access to SELECT or EXAMINE the mailbox.
sections.plainLanguage: The identifiers reveal what is in a mailbox, so a client that may post to a mailbox but not read it should not be told them.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 2359
sections.content:
This document obsoletes RFC 2359, but it is based on that document and takes substantial text from it, with numerous clarifications in the wording.

RFC 2359 implied that a server must always return COPYUID and APPENDUID data, and therefore suggested that in such cases the server should return arbitrary data if the destination mailbox did not support persistent UIDs. This document adds the UIDNOTSTICKY response code to say that a mailbox does not support persistent UIDs, and stipulates that a UIDPLUS server does not return COPYUID or APPENDUID data when the destination of the COPY or APPEND has UIDNOTSTICKY status. The document also constitutes the registration of the UIDPLUS capability in the imap4-capabilities registry, replacing RFC 2359.
sections.plainLanguage: The 2005 version fixes the awkward part of the earlier one. Before, a server had to answer with something even when it could not know the identifiers; now it says so plainly instead.

S: * 3 EXPUNGE

items.title: APPENDUID
items.text: The UIDVALIDITY of the destination mailbox and the UID the appended message was given. Returned in a tagged OK to APPEND.

items.title: COPYUID
items.text: The UIDVALIDITY of the destination mailbox, the UIDs of the messages copied, and the UIDs they were given. Returned in a tagged OK to COPY.

items.title: UIDNOTSTICKY
items.text: The mailbox cannot keep UIDs between sessions. Returned in an untagged NO to SELECT.

messages.label: APPEND saved-messages
messages.note: One message is appended to the mailbox.

messages.label: COPY 2:4 meeting
messages.note: Three messages are copied into another mailbox.

messages.label: OK [COPYUID 38505 304,319:320 3956:3958]
messages.note: The source UIDs and the new destination UIDs.

messages.label: UID COPY 305:310 meeting
messages.note: Those UIDs do not exist, so nothing is copied.
